name: SDC Games
description: A 2-day multi-domain challenge covering AI/ML, Coding, Cyber Security, Web Development, Design, and PR. Day 1 tests multiple independent wings; Day 2 combines finalists into common cross-domain scenario challenges.
rules: Day 1 has 3 technical rounds + 1 non-technical fun round. Participants cannot pick the same technical domain twice on Day 1. Top scorers advance to Day 2.

name: Smash Karts
teamSize: 4 for people making their own cars, 1 for people competing without their own car
description: The competition is split into 2 categories: People who come with their own cars (knockout bracket) and people who would like to learn even without their own car through hands-on rounds involving C++ microcontroller code debugging, sensor wiring, and a power-up lap race.
rules:
Bracket system for people who bring their own cars. 3 rounds for people who can’t afford to make the car:
Round 1 - Microcontroller code correction
Round 2 - Wiring Sensors to the microcontroller using schematic diagram
Round 3 - Race the car on the track
poc: Krishnanarayanan M (+91 98460 32569), Kallavi Sree Sathya Sivani (+91 7396292887)

name: Impact Tank
description: IMPACT TANK is a structured student startup challenge taking participants from problem identification through prototype building, market validation, and go-to-market planning, culminating in an offline finale at NIT Warangal with interactive prototype demos at Impact Expo and an executive pitch.
rules: Shortlisted teams first showcase interactive, live demonstrations of their prototypes at the Impact Expo, followed by a final pitch presentation and Q&A session before an expert panel.

name: Chem-E-Car Showdown
description: Build a car powered entirely by chemistry — no batteries, no motors, and no mechanical brakes. Teams design a small vehicle propelled by a chemical reaction of their choice, and engineer a second reaction to stop it precisely. Target distance and payload are revealed just an hour before the run.
rules: Max car dimension: 40x30x20 cm. No commercial batteries or mechanical stopping devices. Scored on stopping precision relative to the target line.

name: DEFCON
description: A live attack-and-defense cybersecurity hackathon. Every team is assigned a machine to patch and protect while simultaneously probing and compromising rival team targets across a live local network.
rules: Round 1 (Fortify): Inspect and patch assigned machine. Round 2 (Attack): Network opens for offensive exploitation. No DoS or attack on competitor host workstations allowed.

name: Edge Olympics
description: EdgeAI-based constrained hardware challenge where participants solve real-world problem statements and deploy optimized solutions on resource-limited hardware.
rules: Refer to official guideline document: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1fBSquLyHFpFusrW8Y3tMv7y8OqaoDCrp2Xlr8lIZg-E/edit?usp=sharing

name: MECHATRONICS GALA
description: Flagship multi-tier robotics showcase featuring Turing Track (autonomous 1:10 scale car racing), Mach Sprint (obstacle drone racing with provided ESP32 Litewing drones), and AI Gambit (human vs 6-DOF robotic arm).
rules: Refer to official event folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1apzGkzXSAwg4MwAMcDPtMd_VqwAjeTFX?usp=drive_link

name: RoboCannonade
description: Motorized table-tennis ball launcher shootout. External participants custom-build their robot over a month; internal NITW teams get a 1-hour sprint to assemble and code using a provided standardized kit.
rules: Stationary robot with at least 3-DOF. Wireless or autonomous firing at targets across close, medium, and long ranges. Autonomous targeting awards massive bonus multipliers.

name: RUBE WARS
description: A team-based engineering challenge where teams design and build a continuous chain-reaction machine achieving a target using at least 6 and at most 9 mechanisms chosen from a provided list of 15.
rules: Single round. 45-60 minutes build & test time. Machines must execute seamlessly from a single trigger with zero manual intervention. Scored out of 100 on target completion, reliability, and creativity.

name: the engineering challenge
description: A fast-paced multi-station circuit of quick engineering puzzles, micro-prototyping challenges, and hands-on games designed to test practical intuition.
rules: 4 to 5 challenge stations. Points awarded for completion speed and accuracy across all stations.

name: ARCADE
description: Interactive robotics and embedded-systems challenge comprising two events: writing autonomous tracking & paddle algorithms for AI Air Hockey, and trajectory prediction for Robot Strike.
rules: Participants develop control logic/algorithms, validate in MATLAB simulation, and deploy directly onto real-time robotic hardware (Raspberry Pi/ESP).

name: AI Unveiled
description: Suite of interactive AI challenges: Motion Rush (MediaPipe body-tracking gaming), Clash of Minds (half-duplex AI debate), LLM Jailbreak (prompt injection defense bypass), and LLM Multi-Agent Orchestration.
rules: Participants compete across challenges to accumulate points on a unified normalized leaderboard. Goodies and prizes for top scorers.

name: KBC - Kaun Banega Crorepati
description: A knowledge quiz event modelled on the iconic TV game show testing trivia knowledge, quick thinking, and composure under pressure on the Hot Seat with lifelines and progressive stakes.
rules: Round 1 (Fastest Fingers First): 5 numbered options arranged in correct order via SMS. Round 2 (Hot Seat): Standard KBC-style MCQs vs Quizmaster. Lifelines: 50:50, Audience Poll, Phone a Friend, Double Dip.

name: MUSIC CORNER
description: Interactive musical performance combining guitar, drums, and piano sounds using technology: an Arduino UNO + MPU6050 Air Guitar, a 555-timer synthesizer, and an ESP32 wearable motion-controlled Air Drum kit.
rules: Hands-on exhibition and demonstration conducted to entertain and engage participants.

name: 60 Seconds: Chemical Apocalypse
description: An intense simulation where teams step into an emergency disaster response role after a sudden chemical leak. Teams conduct a 60-second material scramble, construct protective gear, isolate valves, and manage crises under pressure.
rules: Phase 1: 60-second material scramble (max 2 items per run). Phase 2: Crisis Management (Rounds 1–4). Phase 3: 60-second internal trading window. Phase 4: Advanced Scenarios & External Visitor trade verification.

name: SpaceWars
description: Virtual gaming experience using physical gauntlet-style controller gloves. Features drone piloting, alien defense, and haptic feedback where participants physically feel enemy hits and attacks.
rules: Individual or 1v1 quick rounds on dedicated stations.

name: Vehicle Demonstration
description: Showcase powered by 4 student vehicle teams (Team Mechaholics, Team Spardhak, Team Mechxhausters, and Team Ashvaratha) presenting custom quad-bikes, ATVs, Formula race cars, and go-karts.
rules: Touching the vehicles without the permission of the respective team members is strictly prohibited.

name: Saponify and Aroma Lab
description: Two hands-on chemistry workshops: Saponify lets participants formulate and mold their own glycerin soap bar, while Aroma Lab teaches fragrance pyramid blending to formulate a custom 10 ml roll-on perfume.
rules: Conducted in batches of 25 from 10 AM to 5 PM. Non-competitive hands-on learning. Every participant takes home what they make and receives a certificate.

name: Mech Tag
description: Structured zero-contact 3v3 laser tag tournament inside a custom arena with dynamic scoring, hit deductions, anti-camping protocols, and scattered hidden objects to retrieve under fire.
rules: Fixed obstacles cannot be moved or climbed. Clear line of sight required (no blind firing). 20-30s maximum camping rule per cover spot.

name: Business Frenzy
description: Interactive business simulation where teams assemble a flagship smartphone using feature cards, trade components, navigate unforeseen market shocks and technology auctions, and pitch to judges.
rules: Fixed virtual budget. Multiple rounds of card trading, auctioning new tech cards after sudden market news, followed by final product lock-in and a pitch presentation.
poc: Arushi Pundir (9068944236), Tushar Jain (9864512346), Anurag Sharma (9815880722)

name: Forensic Investigation
description: Full-scale crime scene investigation. Teams enter an evidence-filled room, inspect latent fingerprints, reveal invisible ink via UV light, analyze chromatography results, and submit their deduction verdict.
rules: 15 minutes inside the staged crime scene room for evidence gathering, followed immediately by 15 minutes in the writing room to formulate and submit findings.

name: CSES Arcade
description: Two-day hybrid event beginning with an interactive gaming arcade showcase, transitioning into an intensive Reinforcement Learning (RL) hackathon to train an agent capable of mastering and beating the featured games.
rules: Games code released at 6 PM Day 1. Online development until 9 AM Day 2, followed by on-site final training and presentations. Scored primarily on test win-rate.

name: Warangal Trading Ring 2.0
description: High-intensity live market simulation condensing 5 trading days into 90 minutes. Participants manage ₹10,00,000 virtual capital across 15–20 real-time fluctuating commodities, equities, and market shocks.
rules: Dynamic trading window over 5 simulated trading cycles. Evaluation based on risk management, strategy, and net portfolio return.

name: Venture Vortex
description: All-India startup strategy contest: Round 1 analyzes strategic teardowns of 50 top startups; Round 2 develops an MVP or marketing deck; Round 3 brings finalists into an executive boardroom pitch at NIT Warangal.
rules: Rounds 1 & 2 conducted online. Shortlisted teams present live in Round 3 (5–10 min presentation + 15 min Q&A with investor/expert panel).

name: ECO CITY
description: Browser-based sustainability strategy simulation where teams spend a budget to balance power, pollution, housing, and food to keep their city surviving over a simulated 300-year horizon.
rules: 30-minute design/spending window. Engine immediately simulates survival year-by-year upon submission. Winner decided by longest survival time and lowest peak pollution.

name: ∑ o poly
description: Strategy mathematical board game where players acquire mathematical milestones, manage asset portfolios, and solve procedural quantitative problems across pure math, computing, and calculus sectors.
rules: Round 1: Unstop logic/math quiz. Round 2: Mass digital board game phase. Round 3: Top 16 finalists compete live on-site at NIT Warangal.

name: Delta Code
description: Computational mathematics competition testing algorithms and Python implementation across Graph Theory, Information Theory, Probability & Statistics, Linear Algebra, and Number Theory.
rules: Round 1: Online prelims on Unstop. Round 2: Domain-specific problem solving with Python (NumPy, SciPy, SymPy) followed by an online methodology presentation.

name: Metamagic
description: Interactive metallurgy exhibition where participants cycle through stations to observe shape-memory alloys, smart materials, crystal microstructures, and property relationships.
rules: Walk-in interactive exploratory demonstration open to all branches.

name: Aim for the best
description: A dart challenge merged with Marvel & DC material trivia. Players aim at metal-labeled sectors (Steel, Aluminium, Copper, Zinc, Lead) and answer pop-culture metallurgy questions for bonus multipliers.
rules: Each team throws 5 darts. Scoring based on hit metal sector and correctness of subsequent comic/materials question.

name: Meta Armor
description: Thermal protection system design challenge where teams build a lightweight, low-cost thermal shield for a space re-entry capsule model and test it against a standardized high-heat source.
rules: 10-minute design & budget phase -> 20-minute physical construction -> standard flame/heat test -> failure analysis & rapid re-test.

name: Neural Core (Mind controlled challenge)
description: Brainwave-controlled ferrofluid exhibit. Participants wear an EEG headset and must maintain intense cognitive concentration for 10 seconds to energize an electromagnetic array that sprouts spikes in the ferrofluid chamber.
rules: Solo challenge. Real-time EEG brainwave feedback and focus levels are projected on an external spectator display.

name: Bid to Build
description: Civil engineering structural challenge where teams budget and bid on raw building materials, construct a load-bearing prototype, and undergo ultimate stress testing.
rules: Round 1: Resource auction/bidding. Round 2: Timed model fabrication. Models are scored on load-bearing efficiency, cost management, and structural stability.

name: INTO THE VOID
description: A VR experience where technology meets thrill, fear, and fun. Participants step into a virtual world of unexpected challenges, intense situations, and terrifying surprises designed to deliver a memorable death-scare experience. Combines immersive VR technology, interactive hardware, and pure adrenaline.
rules: Each participant plays the VR game individually within a fixed time limit and must follow the coordinators' instructions. Running, jumping, sudden movements, or misuse of the VR equipment are not allowed. Participants may stop at any time if they feel uncomfortable or unwell. Respect the equipment and other players; the coordinators' decision is final.

name: Jahaaz
description: Flagship nautical event set at the central fountain in front of the Main Building. Custom-engineered RC boats (ESP32, 380 DC motor, 30A brushed ESC, MG90S servo rudder, 2S LiPo) navigate an aquatic arena with floating PVC borders, plywood chicanes, and plastic lining. Three stages: a speed sprint time trial, an obstacle slalom, and a head-to-head elimination final through active fountain sprays.
rules: Team of 3 participants, 1 RC boat per team. Navigate the water maze and complete designated checkpoints. Solve puzzles and Dynamic QR challenges to unlock the next clues. Collect the required electronic components, use them to complete the final circuit, and decode the final Morse-code message. Points are awarded for tasks, puzzles, QR challenges, components, final challenges and time; the highest total valid score wins. No interference, external assistance, QR sharing/tampering or unauthorised shortcuts. Follow all organiser and marshal instructions; only approved equipment may be used. Detailed scoring, technical requirements and procedures are explained at the official briefing.

name: Model Hovercraft Challenge
description: Combines learning with practical engineering. In the workshop phase, teams learn hovercraft mechanics and build working models; in the competition phase, they race their hovercrafts through different challenge tracks. Teaches air lift, thrust, reduced friction, and steering control.
rules:
Participants should be engineering or technically skilled college students. Team size 4-5 (organiser may set a hard maximum); each participant may compete for only one team; teams must register beforehand and submit a team name.
Phase 1 - Workshop (Oct 25): guided session; each team builds a hovercraft from the standard kit and must complete it to qualify.
Phase 2 - On-site assembly & safety (Oct 31): kit build check (~2 hrs) with custom-designed skirt, body and steering, and no parts outside the official kit; testing & setup (~30 mins) of air cushion, thrust and steering, plus a mandatory safety check.
Phase 3 - Competition rounds (~2-3 hrs): Race (fastest time), Obstacle Course (minimum penalties), Water Race (fastest time), Precision Landing (stop closest to the target mark).
Phase 4 - Results (~30 mins): scores from all 4 tracks are added, judges score design quality and team presentation, and the highest total wins Hovercraft Champion.

name: Glow Wall
description: Hands-on activity based on phosphorescence. Participants use UV light to draw, write, and create patterns on a specially prepared phosphorescent wall; exposed areas glow brightly and fade over time. Try equations, constellations, wave patterns, symbols, drawings, or temporary silhouettes by blocking the UV light.
rules: Only the UV lights and materials provided by the organisers may be used. UV lights must be used only on the designated Glow Wall and must not be directed towards another participant's face or eyes. Designs must be appropriate for a college event, with no offensive or inappropriate content.

name: Natural Disaster Resilience Track
description: National-level engineering design challenge where teams work on a problem for a month, then present and demonstrate at the fest. Teams design, build, simulate and test solutions against disaster scenarios (floods, earthquakes, cyclones, landslides). Five problem statements; each team may enter any two. PS-01 Flood Vault: reusable watertight enclosure (max 17x17x15 cm, 750 g) protecting a buzzer circuit and tissue indicator through a 10-minute submersion. PS-02 Ground Zero: build and optimize an FE model of an earthquake-resistant structure (ANSYS, Abaqus, SAP2000, ETABS, OpenSees, MATLAB etc.) under a common baseline and ground motion. PS-03 Survivor Seeker: battery-powered search-and-rescue rover (max 30 cm cube, 5 kg) that detects survivors, crosses ramps, debris, gravel, narrow passages and muddy/waterlogged terrain, and reaches the rescue zone fastest. PS-04 EvacSim: Python/MATLAB tool planning evacuation of a cyclone-hit coastal city (routes, shelters, evacuation time, bottlenecks, resources). PS-05 Student Innovation Challenge: define your own disaster-resilience problem and deliver an original prototype and/or simulation. Prizes: ₹7,000 for 1st and ₹3,500 for 2nd.
rules: Each team may enter up to two of the five problem statements, each judged independently. Per challenge, submit a Design Report (max 5 pages), an Engineering Development Log (Excel), and CAD files with an assembly drawing (PS-04 submits source code and the simulation model instead). Each team gives a 3-minute technical presentation before testing. Single live round per challenge: PS-01 is a 10-minute submersion test, PS-03 is a timed obstacle course, and PS-02, PS-04 and PS-05 are evaluated on analysis and presentation.

name: Shark Tank 3.0 (NITW Edition)
description: Innovation-driven competition where participants turn real-world problems (science, technology, healthcare, sustainability, engineering, education, etc.) into practical, technology-driven solutions. Teams select a problem, research its root causes, propose a feasible, research-backed solution, and build a working functional prototype. Shortlisted teams pitch before a jury, explaining the problem, uniqueness, technology and methodology, feasibility, scalability and impact. Judged on innovation, technical execution, problem-solving approach, functionality, practicality, and presentation.
rules: Flow: 1. Registration. 2. Problem statement selection. 3. Research and problem analysis. 4. Solution ideation and design. 5. Working functional prototype development. 6. Final presentation and prototype demonstration. 7. Jury evaluation and Q&A. 8. Results announcement and prize distribution.

name: Deconstruct AI
description: Three-round competition combining prompt engineering, reverse engineering, mathematical logic, and research-based implementation. Round 1 (Prompt to Pixel): recreate a complex reference image with AI image-generation tools in limited attempts. Round 2 (The Black Box Challenge): reverse-engineer the rule behind input-output examples across five questions of increasing difficulty. Round 3 (Research to Reality): understand a research paper and implement its proposed solution or a functional proof of concept using AI/ML.
rules: 1. Registration per the announced eligibility and team-size requirements. 2. Round 1: closest visual matches (fixed number of attempts) qualify. 3. Round 2: five problems; ranked by correct answers, ties broken by time taken. 4. Round 3: analyse a research paper and implement its solution or proof of concept. 5. Final evaluation on implementation, technical understanding, accuracy, innovation, and presentation. 6. Winners announced based on the final evaluation.
